text:
CRM Developer reports the Atlas closeout is complete in the CRM. Customer 54 (Ryne Bell) renamed Atlas Skin to Atlas Eternal across company and brand. Quote Q-0046 marked Accepted. Q-2005 client name updated. A completion note was added stating the manufacturing contract was sent to Ryne via WhatsApp, ref PI-2026-0802. No open Atlas task or deal existed; tasks 234 and 310 were already done. Database backed up before changes.

CONSULTANT NOTE - NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. The CRM browser session is logged out, so none of these claims could be live-checked. Reported as the agent stated, not as confirmed.

TWO ITEMS FLAGGED FOR SAM:
1. The note says the Atlas Eternal manufacturing contract was already sent to Ryne via WhatsApp. That contract is on hold awaiting Sam's approval and its pro forma still carries three unfilled placeholders (fill size/packaging, billing address, lead time/Incoterms). Sam must confirm whether he sent it himself. If an agent sent an unapproved document to a customer, that is a policy breach requiring immediate review.
2. Three duplicate PI-2026-0802 pro forma records exist (ids 24, 25, 26), all still draft. Duplicates on a live quote risk double-invoicing a customer. Needs cleanup to a single record - Sam's approval required before deleting CRM data.

Also noted: no manufacturing contract document is stored in the CRM at all. The signed-agreement trail lives only in the agent filesystem.
spoken_text: Sam, the CRM Developer says the Atlas closeout is done. Ryne Bell's company is renamed to Atlas Eternal, quote Q-0046 is marked accepted, and the stale Atlas Skin name is cleared. I could not verify any of that live, because the CRM session is logged out, so I'm passing it along as claimed rather than confirmed. Two things concern me. The completion note says the Atlas Eternal manufacturing contract was already sent to Ryne over WhatsApp, but that contract is still waiting on your approval and its pro forma has three blanks in it. I need you to tell me whether you sent that yourself. There are also three duplicate pro forma records on the same invoice number, all still draft, which could double-invoice him. My recommendation is that you confirm the contract question first, then log me back into the CRM so I can verify the rest properly.
